newsitem.title: USA: Demand rise backs stronger US grade differentials.
newsitem.headline: Demand rise backs stronger US grade differentials.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes continued to peg slightly firmer prices Wednesday afternoon, supported by gasoline paper market buying on supportive weekly inventory data.
Cash traders said there was stronger demand noted in the U.S. Gulf for domestic and foreign grades, propping differentials to higher numbers.
For outright June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, the latest prices were seen around 15 cts higher at $19.75-85 a barrel, down slightly from late morning levels.
June/July spreads were only a shade wider, at around 8 cts in favor of the second month July month. Traders said June Postings remained at $1.85-1.90.
Deals for sweet grades were seen at stronger numbers, reflective of the lack of North Sea competition for the immediate-term.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talked at a 5-10 cts premium to WTI, after trading as firm as WTI/Cushing +8 cts.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was sold at 35 and 38 cts under the benchmark, with Midland/WTI wavering at a 31-30 cts discount heading into mid-afternoon.
Sours firmed a shade, with major U.S. Gulf refiners selling barrels actively around a $1.55-50 discount. Eugene Island was talked at WTI/Cushing minus $1.35-25.
